Idempotent loads (stage plus MERGE, or truncate-and-reload) ensure reruns produce correct results without duplicating partially loaded rows.

Reference: Reliable load patterns - Microsoft Fabric
questions.extraHtml: Plain reruns of a non-idempotent load can duplicate rows. Randomizing keys corrupts identity and hides duplicates. Idempotent design makes reruns safe.

questions.promptHtml: A dashboard built on an Eventhouse must update within seconds of new events for a live operations view. Which combination best supports low-latency dashboards?

options.label: A nightly batch refresh feeding an import semantic model so the dashboard loads from a static daily snapshot
A OneLake shortcut to cold archive storage queried on demand whenever a user opens the operations view
A real-time KQL/Eventhouse source with a real-time dashboard or Direct Query so new events appear within seconds

questions.correctLabel: A real-time KQL/Eventhouse source with a real-time dashboard or Direct Query so new events appear within seconds
questions.rationaleHtml:
Pairing Eventhouse with real-time dashboards keeps latency in seconds, unlike batch import snapshots or cold-archive queries.

Reference: Real-time dashboards - Microsoft Fabric
questions.extraHtml: Nightly import is minutes-to-hours stale. Cold archive is slow and not real-time. A real-time Eventhouse-backed dashboard meets the seconds-latency goal.

questions.promptHtml: You must confirm a Dataflow Gen2 actually wrote the expected number of rows to its Lakehouse destination after each refresh. Where do you review these run details?

options.label: The Dataflow Gen2 refresh history and run details, which report status, duration, and rows written per run
The Git commit history, which shows the dataflow's saved query definition but not its per-run row counts or status
The workspace settings page, which controls permissions and defaults rather than execution run outcomes

questions.correctLabel: The Dataflow Gen2 refresh history and run details, which report status, duration, and rows written per run
questions.rationaleHtml:
Dataflow refresh history and run details show outcomes including status and rows processed, confirming each refresh's result.

Reference: Monitor Dataflow Gen2 - Microsoft Fabric
questions.extraHtml: Git history stores definitions, not run metrics. Workspace settings manage configuration, not runs. Dataflow refresh/run details provide execution outcomes.

questions.promptHtml: A Warehouse experiences slow queries because a frequently filtered large table is not physically clustered by the filter column. Which optimization best improves selective query performance?

options.label: Order or cluster the data by the frequently filtered key so scans skip irrelevant data during selective queries
Remove all filters from the analytic queries so the engine reads sequentially and avoids random lookups entirely
Cast the filter column to a string so more values match and the optimizer can reuse a broader cached result

questions.correctLabel: Order or cluster the data by the frequently filtered key so scans skip irrelevant data during selective queries
questions.rationaleHtml:
Physically ordering/clustering by the common filter key improves data skipping, so selective queries scan far less data.

Reference: Performance guidelines - Microsoft Fabric
questions.extraHtml: Removing filters increases scanned data. Casting to string widens matches and defeats selectivity. Clustering by the filter key enables data skipping.

questions.promptHtml: An Eventhouse retains far more raw data than analysts ever query, inflating cost. Which optimization reduces storage cost while keeping recent data queryable?

options.label: Disable ingestion during business hours so less data accumulates while analysts are actively querying it
Export the whole database to CSV weekly and delete everything so nothing is retained beyond the export
Configure a retention (caching and retention) policy so old data ages out or moves to cheaper storage automatically

questions.correctLabel: Configure a retention (caching and retention) policy so old data ages out or moves to cheaper storage automatically
questions.rationaleHtml:
Retention and caching policies control how long data is kept hot and when it expires, balancing query needs against storage cost.

Reference: Retention policies - Microsoft Fabric
questions.extraHtml: Pausing ingestion loses events and does not address stored history. Wholesale export-and-delete destroys queryability. Retention policies automate cost-aware data aging.

questions.promptHtml: A notebook job in a pipeline succeeds but the pipeline reports success even when the notebook logically failed a data-quality check. How should the notebook signal failure to the pipeline?

options.label: Print an error message to the notebook output and trust the pipeline to parse the text and fail accordingly
Add a long sleep at the end of the notebook so the pipeline times out and is therefore treated as failed
Use notebookutils/mssparkutils to exit with a failure status (or raise) so the pipeline activity is marked failed

questions.correctLabel: Use notebookutils/mssparkutils to exit with a failure status (or raise) so the pipeline activity is marked failed
questions.rationaleHtml:
Signaling failure via an explicit exit/error (for example mssparkutils.notebook.exit or raising) makes the pipeline activity fail deterministically.

Reference: Notebook utilities - Microsoft Fabric
questions.extraHtml: Pipelines do not parse printed text for failure. Forcing a timeout via sleep is hacky and unreliable. Exit with a real failure status to propagate the error.

questions.promptHtml: A team wants column-level access enforced consistently whether users query a Lakehouse table via the SQL endpoint or read it through OneLake. Which mechanism enforces access at the OneLake data layer itself?

options.label: OneLake security data access roles that enforce column-level restrictions across engines reading the item in OneLake
SQL analytics endpoint GRANT/DENY statements, which apply only to T-SQL sessions and not to direct OneLake reads
Power BI report-level filters that hide columns visually while leaving the underlying OneLake data fully readable

questions.correctLabel: OneLake security data access roles that enforce column-level restrictions across engines reading the item in OneLake
questions.rationaleHtml:
OneLake security applies access controls at the data layer, so restrictions hold across engines that read the item directly from OneLake.

Reference: OneLake security - Microsoft Fabric
questions.extraHtml: SQL endpoint grants only cover T-SQL access, not direct OneLake reads. Report filters are cosmetic. OneLake security enforces access at the data layer across engines.

questions.promptHtml: You must ensure only a specific Spark runtime version and preinstalled libraries are used across all notebooks in a workspace for reproducibility. Where is this best standardized?

options.label: In each notebook, by asking authors to pip install the same packages at the top of every single notebook run
In an environment attached to the workspace/pool that pins the runtime and libraries for all sessions to use
In the deployment pipeline, so only production notebooks receive the pinned runtime while others drift freely

questions.correctLabel: In an environment attached to the workspace/pool that pins the runtime and libraries for all sessions to use
questions.rationaleHtml:
Fabric environments capture runtime version, libraries, and Spark settings, giving reproducible, standardized sessions across notebooks.

Reference: Fabric environments - Microsoft Fabric
questions.extraHtml: Per-notebook installs drift and are error-prone. Pinning only in production leaves development inconsistent. A shared environment standardizes runtime and libraries everywhere.

questions.promptHtml: A pipeline must pass the output row count from a Lookup activity into a later Set Variable and then into a notebook parameter. Which mechanism carries the value between activities?

options.label: Reference the Lookup activity output using a dynamic expression to set the variable and pass it as a parameter
Hardcode the expected row count into the notebook so the value is always available without any expressions
Write the row count to a text file and have every downstream activity re-open and parse the file each time

questions.correctLabel: Reference the Lookup activity output using a dynamic expression to set the variable and pass it as a parameter
questions.rationaleHtml:
Dynamic expressions read a prior activity's output (for example @activity('Lookup').output) to flow values into variables and parameters.

Reference: Expressions and functions - Microsoft Fabric
questions.extraHtml: Hardcoding breaks when counts change. Round-tripping through a file adds fragile I/O. Dynamic expressions natively pass activity outputs downstream.

questions.promptHtml: To limit blast radius, a data engineer should have edit rights only in the Development workspace and read-only access in Production. How do you implement least privilege here?

options.label: Assign Contributor on Development and Viewer on Production so edits are isolated to the non-production stage
Grant the engineer Admin on both workspaces so they can fix anything quickly if a production incident occurs at any hour
Put both workspaces under one role assignment set to Member to keep permission management simple overall

questions.correctLabel: Assign Contributor on Development and Viewer on Production so edits are isolated to the non-production stage
questions.rationaleHtml:
Scoping edit rights to Development (Contributor) and read-only to Production (Viewer) enforces least privilege and protects production.

Reference: Workspace roles - Microsoft Fabric
questions.extraHtml: Admin everywhere over-grants and risks production. A single Member role for both allows unwanted production edits. Per-stage roles enforce least privilege.

questions.promptHtml: A KQL database must restrict which rows analysts see based on their team, applied at query time within the Eventhouse. Which feature provides this row filtering?

options.label: Dynamic data masking, which obscures individual field values but does not remove entire rows from results
Column-level security, which blocks specific columns rather than filtering the rows an analyst can see
A KQL row level security policy that filters returned rows according to the querying user's identity or role

questions.correctLabel: A KQL row level security policy that filters returned rows according to the querying user's identity or role
questions.rationaleHtml:
KQL databases support row level security policies that transparently filter query results per the user's identity, similar to warehouse RLS.

Reference: Row level security in KQL - Microsoft Fabric
questions.extraHtml: Masking hides values, not rows. Column-level security removes columns, not rows. A KQL RLS policy performs the row-scoped filtering.

questions.promptHtml: A pipeline should skip its main load when an upstream validation activity reports zero new files, but proceed when files exist. Which construct implements this conditional branching?

options.label: A ForEach activity that iterates the file list so the loop body simply does nothing when the list is empty anyway
An If Condition activity evaluating the file count expression to choose the load branch versus a skip branch
A Wait activity that pauses long enough that any missing files are guaranteed to arrive before loading

questions.correctLabel: An If Condition activity evaluating the file count expression to choose the load branch versus a skip branch
questions.rationaleHtml:
The If Condition activity branches on a boolean expression, running the load only when the condition (files exist) is true.

Reference: Control flow activities - Microsoft Fabric
questions.extraHtml: ForEach can iterate but does not cleanly model a proceed/skip decision with separate branches. Wait just delays and does not decide. If Condition is the branching construct.

questions.promptHtml: A workspace uses a custom Spark pool, but jobs still start slowly during the day. You want faster session startup while keeping the pool's isolation. Which setting helps most?

options.label: Increase the pool's maximum node count so that larger clusters inherently eliminate the cold-start delay
Disable autoscale entirely so the pool never resizes and therefore never spends time provisioning nodes
Enable high concurrency and keep sessions/pool warm settings so ready capacity reduces per-job startup time

questions.correctLabel: Enable high concurrency and keep sessions/pool warm settings so ready capacity reduces per-job startup time
questions.rationaleHtml:
High concurrency session sharing and keeping capacity warm reduce startup latency on custom pools without abandoning isolation.

Reference: High concurrency - Microsoft Fabric
questions.extraHtml: Bigger max nodes does not remove the initial provisioning wait. Disabling autoscale fixes size, not warm readiness. High concurrency and warm capacity cut startup latency.

questions.promptHtml: A regulated dataset requires that even workspace admins cannot read certain columns unless explicitly authorized at the data layer. Which control enforces this beyond workspace roles?

options.label: Workspace role tuning, since demoting admins to Members automatically prevents them from reading the columns
OneLake security column-level restrictions that apply at the data layer independent of workspace role level
Sensitivity labels, which classify the data and therefore block admins from reading the labeled columns

questions.correctLabel: OneLake security column-level restrictions that apply at the data layer independent of workspace role level
questions.rationaleHtml:
OneLake security enforces column access at the data layer, so authorization is independent of, and not overridden by, workspace admin roles.

Reference: OneLake security - Microsoft Fabric
questions.extraHtml: Adjusting workspace roles still leaves broad access and is not column-scoped. Sensitivity labels classify but do not block reads. OneLake data-layer security enforces the restriction.

questions.promptHtml: You need to grant a partner team access to just one specific report in a workspace without giving them access to the rest of the workspace items. What is the correct approach?

options.label: Share the specific item directly with per-item permissions instead of granting a broad workspace role
Add the partner team as workspace Viewers so they can open the one report along with everything else present
Move the report into the partner's own capacity so capacity boundaries limit them to that single item

questions.correctLabel: Share the specific item directly with per-item permissions instead of granting a broad workspace role
questions.rationaleHtml:
Item-level sharing grants access to a single item without exposing the whole workspace, satisfying least privilege.

Reference: Share Fabric items - Microsoft Fabric
questions.extraHtml: Workspace Viewer exposes all items, over-granting. Capacity boundaries govern compute, not item access. Item-level sharing scopes access to just the report.

questions.promptHtml: A team wants their curated gold Lakehouse tables to be easily found and trusted by analysts across the company, signaling they are self-service ready but not officially certified. Which action fits?

options.label: Apply the Certified endorsement, which is the appropriate self-service signal any author can set on their own tables
Apply the Promoted endorsement to highlight the tables as recommended, self-service content for broader discovery
Assign a Confidential sensitivity label, since classification is what makes tables discoverable and trusted

questions.correctLabel: Apply the Promoted endorsement to highlight the tables as recommended, self-service content for broader discovery
questions.rationaleHtml:
Promoted is the self-service endorsement authors can apply to signal recommended content, improving discovery short of formal certification.

Reference: Promote content - Microsoft Fabric
questions.extraHtml: Certified is controlled by authorized certifiers, not self-service. Sensitivity labels classify confidentiality, not trust/discovery. Promoted is the self-service recommendation signal.

questions.promptHtml: A pipeline must fail fast and stop remaining activities the moment a critical validation activity fails, rather than continuing other branches. How do you model this?

options.label: Connect subsequent critical activities with On success dependencies so failure halts that dependent path immediately
Use On completion dependencies everywhere so activities always run regardless of upstream success or failure
Remove all dependencies so every activity runs in parallel and failures never block anything downstream

questions.correctLabel: Connect subsequent critical activities with On success dependencies so failure halts that dependent path immediately
questions.rationaleHtml:
On success precedence means downstream activities run only if the predecessor succeeded, so a failure stops that dependent path.

Reference: Activity dependencies - Microsoft Fabric
questions.extraHtml: On completion runs regardless of failure, which is the opposite of fail-fast. Removing dependencies lets everything run despite failures. On success halts dependents on failure.

questions.promptHtml: A data warehouse table storing customer records must let support agents query it while masking full national ID numbers, yet allow the compliance role to see them unmasked. Which pairing implements this?

options.label: Dynamic data masking on the ID column plus the UNMASK permission granted to the compliance role
Row-level security for agents plus object-level security granting compliance access to the whole table only
Column-level security denying the ID to everyone, then re-granting it to agents but not to compliance

questions.correctLabel: Dynamic data masking on the ID column plus the UNMASK permission granted to the compliance role
questions.rationaleHtml:
DDM masks the ID for general users, while granting UNMASK to compliance lets that role see the real values.

Reference: Dynamic data masking and UNMASK - Microsoft Fabric
questions.extraHtml: RLS filters rows, not values. The CLS option inverts the requirement (agents should be masked, not blocked; compliance should see values). DDM plus UNMASK matches exactly.

questions.promptHtml: A workspace admin wants Spark autoscale so pools grow under load but never exceed a cost ceiling, then shrink when idle. Which configuration meets this?

options.label: A fixed-size pool at the maximum node count, always running the ceiling of nodes to guarantee capacity is ready
A custom pool with autoscale enabled between a minimum and a bounded maximum node count for cost control
The starter pool only, since starter pools give unlimited elastic scaling without any configurable maximum

questions.correctLabel: A custom pool with autoscale enabled between a minimum and a bounded maximum node count for cost control
questions.rationaleHtml:
Autoscale between min and a capped max lets pools grow under load and shrink when idle while enforcing a cost ceiling.

Reference: Autoscale for Spark - Microsoft Fabric
questions.extraHtml: A fixed max-size pool wastes money when idle. Starter pools are convenience-oriented and not the right lever for bounded, cost-controlled autoscale. Custom pool autoscale with a cap fits.

questions.promptHtml: A pipeline copies data from an on-premises SQL Server into a Fabric Lakehouse. Which component enables secure connectivity from Fabric to the on-premises source?

options.label: A OneLake shortcut, which can directly reach on-premises SQL Server over the corporate network without a gateway component
A public endpoint on the SQL Server exposed to the internet so the pipeline can connect to it directly
An on-premises data gateway configured as the connection's gateway so Fabric can reach the private source securely

questions.correctLabel: An on-premises data gateway configured as the connection's gateway so Fabric can reach the private source securely
questions.rationaleHtml:
The on-premises data gateway bridges Fabric to private/on-premises data sources securely without exposing them publicly.

Reference: On-premises data gateway - Microsoft Learn
questions.extraHtml: Shortcuts target cloud object storage, not arbitrary on-prem SQL over a gateway. Exposing a public endpoint is insecure. The data gateway is the secure connectivity component.

questions.promptHtml: Reference data updates rarely but must be joined to a high-volume stream inside an Eventstream to enrich events. Which capability supports enriching streaming events with reference data?

options.label: A tumbling window, because windowing the stream inherently attaches the latest reference values to each event automatically
A VACUUM operation on the reference table so its latest values are pushed into the stream automatically
An Eventstream join/lookup operator that enriches streaming events with the reference dataset during processing

questions.correctLabel: An Eventstream join/lookup operator that enriches streaming events with the reference dataset during processing
questions.rationaleHtml:
Eventstream processing supports joining/looking up reference data to enrich in-flight events before they reach destinations.

Reference: Process events - Microsoft Fabric
questions.extraHtml: Windowing aggregates over time; it does not join reference data. VACUUM is Delta maintenance, unrelated. A join/lookup operator performs the enrichment.

questions.promptHtml: A batch job must upsert incoming changes into a large Delta table, updating existing rows by key and inserting new ones in a single atomic operation. Which Delta feature should you use?

options.label: A MERGE INTO operation that matches on the key to update existing rows and insert new ones atomically
Overwrite the entire table each run so updates and inserts are applied by simply replacing all existing data
Append every incoming row unconditionally and deduplicate later during reporting to simulate an upsert

questions.correctLabel: A MERGE INTO operation that matches on the key to update existing rows and insert new ones atomically
questions.rationaleHtml:
Delta MERGE performs conditional update/insert (and optional delete) by key in one atomic transaction, the standard upsert pattern.

Reference: Delta MERGE upsert - Microsoft Fabric
questions.extraHtml: Full overwrite is wasteful and unsafe for large tables. Append-then-dedup leaves the table dirty. MERGE is the atomic, key-based upsert.

questions.promptHtml: An Eventstream that was streaming events suddenly shows no new data after the source event hub's shared access key was regenerated. What is the most likely cause and fix?

options.label: The Eventstream item was corrupted and must be deleted and rebuilt from scratch to restore the event flow
The stored source connection now has an invalid key, so update the Eventstream source connection with the new key
The workspace capacity is throttling the stream, so pausing every other item will make event delivery resume

questions.correctLabel: The stored source connection now has an invalid key, so update the Eventstream source connection with the new key
questions.rationaleHtml:
When a source secret is rotated, the Eventstream's saved connection breaks; updating the connection credentials restores ingestion.

Reference: Manage Eventstream sources - Microsoft Fabric
questions.extraHtml: Rebuilding the item is unnecessary and disruptive. Capacity throttling would affect processing broadly, not stop a single source right after a key change. Refresh the source connection credentials.

questions.promptHtml: A pipeline loads a Warehouse table slowly because it inserts rows one at a time from a REST source. Which change most improves load throughput?

options.label: Wrap each single-row insert in its own transaction so the engine commits more frequently and stays responsive
Stage the data to files and bulk load into the Warehouse (for example COPY) instead of row-by-row inserts
Add a two-second delay between inserts so the Warehouse is never overwhelmed by concurrent write pressure

questions.correctLabel: Stage the data to files and bulk load into the Warehouse (for example COPY) instead of row-by-row inserts
questions.rationaleHtml:
Bulk/staged loading processes data in large batches, vastly outperforming singleton INSERTs for high-volume loads.

Reference: Ingest data into the Warehouse - Microsoft Fabric
questions.extraHtml: Per-row transactions add commit overhead and slow things further. Adding delays reduces throughput on purpose. Batch/bulk loading is the standard high-throughput ingestion pattern.

questions.promptHtml: You must be notified by email whenever a scheduled semantic model refresh fails, without manually checking each morning. Which configuration achieves this?

options.label: Increase the refresh timeout so failures become rare enough that manual morning checks are sufficient going forward
Add a second identical refresh schedule so that if one refresh fails the other one silently succeeds instead
Enable refresh failure notifications in the semantic model's scheduled refresh settings to email the specified recipients

questions.correctLabel: Enable refresh failure notifications in the semantic model's scheduled refresh settings to email the specified recipients
questions.rationaleHtml:
Scheduled refresh includes a failure notification option that emails owners or a specified list when a refresh fails.

Reference: Refresh failure notifications - Microsoft Learn
questions.extraHtml: A longer timeout does not surface failures or notify anyone. A duplicate schedule wastes capacity and hides the underlying failure. Built-in failure notifications deliver timely alerts.

questions.promptHtml: A recurring Warehouse report query selects every column from a very wide table but the report uses only five columns. Which change most reduces I/O for this query?

options.label: Keep SELECT * but add an ORDER BY so the engine returns the wide result set in a more cache-friendly order
Project only the five needed columns instead of SELECT * so the columnar engine scans far less data
Cast the unused columns to NULL in the query so the engine can skip reading their underlying storage

questions.correctLabel: Project only the five needed columns instead of SELECT * so the columnar engine scans far less data
questions.rationaleHtml:
Selecting only required columns lets the columnar store skip unneeded columns, cutting I/O and speeding the query.

Reference: Warehouse performance guidelines - Microsoft Fabric
questions.extraHtml: Adding ORDER BY increases work and still reads all columns. Casting unused columns to NULL still references them and adds compute. Column projection is the direct I/O reduction.
